# Design

Two waves. Wave 1 is the activation itself in one task, plus a replay of that activation against a copy of a real chain state in a second task that depends on it. Wave 2 runs the chain gates once on the merged wave revision and records what ran.

## The activation plan

The plan name is an exported constant in node/, following the repository's semantic-version naming for upgrade names, and its handler is registered explicitly beside the handlers the embedded tag list registers, so the tag list, the latest upgrade name and every precompile version map stay unchanged.

The plan's store upgrades add exactly the stores the running chain lacks: the custody, anchor, exchange, bridge, launchpad and web-search module stores. The list is static because the store loader runs before any state is readable, and a table test derives the same list from the application's canonical store-key list minus the stores the pre-fork chain carries, so a store added to the application without being added to the plan fails the test.

The handler runs the module manager's migrations once against the version map read from state. Every module the map lacks initialises from its own default genesis exactly once, which brings the web-search module up paused with an empty attestor set and every other module up with its documented default parameters, and then the handler refreshes the web-search precompile entry from state so the block that applies the plan already serves it. It registers no remote asset and creates no denomination.

## Reaching the height

The application's begin blocker calls the scheduling step after the module begin blockers have run, so the upgrade module's own begin blocker has already seen the block with no plan in it and cannot mistake a plan scheduled for the next height for a binary updated before its trigger. At the height one below the fork height, when no plan is scheduled, the plan has no done height and the version map does not already carry every module the plan adds, it schedules the plan for the fork height through the upgrade keeper. Any other height, any already scheduled plan, an already applied plan or a full-genesis chain leaves the store untouched.

At the fork height the application's begin blocker runs before the module begin blockers and, when the scheduled activation plan is due and this process did not start with the plan's upgrade-info.json, writes upgrade-info.json for the plan at that height and stops the node with the SDK's own upgrade-needed message. That is the standard stop: the block is not committed, the last commit is one below the fork height, and the operator restarts the same binary. The restarted process reads the file, mounts the plan's added stores through UpgradeStoreLoader with their initial version equal to the fork height, replays the fork height and lets the upgrade module's begin blocker apply the plan. A height the operator has explicitly marked skipped is left to the upgrade module's own skip path.

The store-loader wiring records, at construction time, that this process started with the activation plan's upgrade-info.json at the fork height and therefore mounted the added stores through the upgrade store loader. That record is the only thing the stop step consults, so the stop happens exactly once per node and the restarted process proceeds.

## Serving the eight

The EVM keeper carries an activation record: one plan name, the module names the plan adds and the precompile addresses the plan brings online. An address named by that record is served when the plan's done height is above zero and the block height is at or above it, or when the chain's module version map already carries every module the plan adds, which is true of every chain started from a full genesis and of no chain that must still apply the plan. An address the record does not name keeps today's rule exactly: served when one of the upgrades it carries a version for was applied at or below the height, or when none of them was ever applied.

The record names all eight addresses the fork brings: the stateless verification precompile, the custody, anchor, exchange, bridge and launchpad module precompiles, the fee-token precompile and the web-search precompile. The record is registered once, when the application builds its custom precompile set, and is not rebuilt when the web-search entry is added to or removed from that set.
